title: One step of the guessing phase
statement: Let $S$ and $V$ be finite deterministic Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$ be an $S$-configuration on $x$ with an active state. For any guessed word $u$ and choice bit $b$, one host step from the guessing-phase configuration associated to $c$ and $u$ yields the guessing-phase configuration associated to the next configuration of the input-normalized machine derived from $S$, with $b$ appended to $u$ precisely when that machine emits a symbol from $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ and $V$ are finite deterministic machines over Booleans
replaced: Let $S, V$ be deterministic machines, $d$ a non-halted scheduler configuration on an input $x$, $u$ a guessed word and $b$ a choice bit. One step of the reverse host under $b$ maps the guessing-phase configuration for $(d,u)$ to the guessing-phase configuration for the stepped configuration of the input-normalized variant of $S$, with $b$ appended to the guessed word exactly when that machine emits at $d$.
